reasons: backend/internal/server/mcpoauth.go:668-680 (needsFetch) + :696-735 (mcpSigningKey): once the key set is older than mcpOAuthKeyTTL (5 min), needsFetch returns true even for a kid the cache already holds, so the request that arrives first performs the JWKS fetch synchronously (up to the 10 s timeout) and every other request in that window — cached kid or not — waits on cache.inflight. With a slow/hung Keycloak this stalls ALL MCP SSO authentication for up to 10 s, then serves the kept keys for the 10 s retry window, then stalls again. Reproduced on HEAD with a probe test: backdate fetched/attempted by TTL+1s, block the fake JWKS handler, send a token with the cached kid → it blocks; a second cached-kid request during that refresh also blocks (>2 s). This violates the campaign rule '보유 중인 kid 는 TTL 이 지났어도 in-flight fetch 를 기다리지 않고 즉시 돌려준다' and only half-fixes the prior rejection's 'a slow/dead Keycloak stalls all MCP auth'. Fix: in mcpSigningKey, under the lock, if cache.issuer==cfg.Issuer and cache.keys[kid] exists, return that key immediately regardless of TTL (do not fetch, do not wait on inflight); keep the fetch/wait path only for unknown kid, nil keys, or issuer change (needsFetch then no longer needs the TTL branch, or the TTL branch applies only when the kid is not cached). Add a test in TestKeyFetchesNeitherBlockOtherTokensNorHammerTheIssuer: after backdate(mcpOAuthKeyTTL+time.Second) with the JWKS handler blocked, a request with the cached kid must answer 200 within ~1 s and must not hit the issuer; then unblock. Update the mcpOAuthKeyCache comment and docs/MCP.md:53 to say when a refresh actually happens.

docs/MCP.md:32: the settings table still says the resource identifier falls back to '요청의 호스트에서 만듭니다(마지막 수단)' when both mcp.oauth.resource and publicUrl are empty. That fallback was deleted in ff47e4e precisely because it let a Host/X-Forwarded-Host-chosen audience pass; the server now goes inactive (metadata 404, plain 401, log 'inactive: no resource identifier'). Replace the clause with: both empty → MCP SSO is inactive and the log/settings card say so; publicUrl cannot be cleared while mcp.oauth.enabled is on without mcp.oauth.resource.
notes: Verified on a throwaway Postgres 16: go test ./... passes (integration tests ran, not skipped); MCP OAuth tests pass under -race -count=3. The new tests copied onto d0a9bdc fail exactly on the three previously rejected defects (X-Forwarded-Host aud → 200; no request_id in refusal logs; cached kid blocked behind fetch; failed fetch retried per request), so the repairs are real and the tests do exercise production wiring (Handler(), real slog text handler into a buffer).

Protected-file checklist: migration 025 is ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS only, default mcp_oauth_enabled=FALSE; the only new unauthenticated routes are the RFC 9728 metadata documents (404 unless active); tokens never create or reactivate accounts (query requires active=TRUE and oidc source); scopes = intersection with the admin ceiling, empty intersection refused, Principal.Has treats empty scopes on ViaAPIKey as nothing; all three ViaAPIKey gates (rbac_policy.go:55, resources.go:399, server.go:419) apply to the SSO principal since ViaAPIKey=true; no KeyID-style gate exists to widen; tokens are not logged (asserted); request_id read from w.Header() matches how requestID middleware stores it; jwks_uri is validated by discoverOIDC; putOIDCSettings validates everything before the single UPDATE.

Secondary (not a reject reason, low probability): in mcpSigningKey the fetch runs with the fetching request's ctx (as the campaign rule requires); if that client disconnects mid-fetch on a cold cache, the resulting context.Canceled is recorded via cache.record as lastErr with attempted=now, so every SSO token gets the cached 503 for the next 10 s. Consider not throttling when errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) and the cancellation came from the caller's ctx.
The repair note's two uncertainties (cold-cache failure cached 10 s; inflight waiter returns 503 on its own ctx cancel) are acceptable design choices and were not counted against the PR.
Frontend/docs additions otherwise match the backend; no secrets exposed in getOIDCSettings (only secretConfigured bool) or the auth config endpoint.
